hint: The equation asks which number, multiplied by itself, makes $25$. There is more than one such number.

hints.text: The equation asks which number, multiplied by itself, makes $25$. There is more than one such number.
Both $5 \times 5$ and $(-5) \times (-5)$ equal $25$, so there are two solutions. The question wants the one above zero.
The solutions are $5$ and $-5$, so the positive solution is $x = 5$.

explanation: Solving $x^2 = 25$ means finding every number whose square is $25$.
Both $5^2 = 25$ and $(-5)^2 = 25$ are true, so the equation has two solutions.
The question asks for the positive one, which is $x = 5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: As a square garden
steps: A square garden has area 25 square meters. Each side is the number that multiplies by itself to give 25.
Side length: 5 meters — lengths are positive, so the garden answer is the positive root.

alternativeExplanations.title: Undo the square
steps: Squaring and square-rooting undo each other, like tying and untying a shoe.
√25 = 5, and its mirror twin −5 also works since a negative times a negative is positive.
